thread:
rebecca_support: Hey team — customer `acme-inc` reporting p95/p99 regressions on streaming responses only. Non-streaming calls look fine. They see big TTFB spikes (~500ms -> 2.1s p99) while total tokens time is stable. Attached a simplified repro and request IDs.

rebecca_support: curl they used: 
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-1","input":"long prompt...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

jordan_se: Thanks. Do we have trace/span IDs for one of the slow requests? Also which protocol were they on (h2 vs SSE over http/1.1)? :eyes:

rebecca_support: They said mobile app using http/2 (okhttp) and web client using EventSource (SSE). Example request id: r-202103-ACME-5f9a. Traces: https://traces.internal/trace/r-202103-ACME-5f9a (logs excerpt below).

rebecca_support: log snippet: 
```
[2026-02-12T14:02:31.123Z] accept req=r-202103-ACME-5f9a conn=cpool-7 latency=2120ms first_chunk=2050ms total=4200ms route=streaming-node-3
[2026-02-12T14:02:31.124Z] backend enqueue batch_id=b-914 size=8 wait=1900ms
[2026-02-12T14:02:31.125Z] flush decision: coalesce window=20ms pooled=true
```

sam_ops: Hmm backend shows large enqueue wait + coalesce window. Could be batching/backpressure issue on that tenant path. Any change in traffic? Also check edge proxy buffering (nginx/h2 proxies sometimes coalesce small chunks).

anya_dev: Can you repro locally with similar QPS and multi-connection mix (h2 + SSE)? If it's coalescing, reducing batch size or flush window might help. We should also check flush heuristics per-model.

mike_eng: I pulled runtime metrics for the time window. Observed continuous batching threshold bumped to 16 tokens for this model after recent optimization (to reduce cost). That increases time-to-first-chunk under low concurrency. For high concurrency it amortizes well but for mixed-protocol clients we see p99 regressions.

mike_eng: snippet from runtime debug: 
```
model: rw-1
batch_policy: dynamic( max_batch=32, min_flush_tokens=16, coalesce_ms=20 )
kv_cache_hits=0 busy_worker=0 queued_requests=7
```

jordan_se: That aligns: min_flush_tokens=16 -> if client expects streaming early chunks, TTFB suffers when prompt tokens < threshold. But why only on some clients? Maybe http/2 multiplexing causes delayed flush vs SSE which relies on smaller chunks — odd it's the reverse here.

sam_ops: Also check edge for `Transfer-Encoding` and `proxy_buffering` settings. Nginx/h2 proxies can buffer chunked responses then release them in coalesced frames. For SSE we often set `proxy_buffering off`. For h2 ensure initial WINDOW_UPDATE isn't starving stream.

rebecca_support: Customer can reproduce reliably on mobile (h2). Web (SSE) shows smaller TTFB but sometimes loses chunk order when network flaps. They prefer streaming though.

anya_dev: Proposed mitigations: 
- Short-term: force non-streaming for that tenant (router rule) until we fix. Quick to deploy.
- Quick test: lower min_flush_tokens to 4 for rw-1 for that tenant and reduce coalesce_ms to 5. Canary to 1% then 10%.
- Medium: add per-client-protocol flush heuristic: if upstream indicates http/2 client, flush earlier (aggressive small-chunk mode).
- Long-term: expose SDK flag so clients can request `prefer_low_ttfb` and we adapt batching.

mike_eng: I can spin canary with lowered flush for tenant `acme-inc` and add additional logging for `first_chunk_wait` and `coalesce_events`. Will do 1% now.

infra-bot: deploy triggered by mike_eng: canary/flush-tweak -> rollout 1% on dedicated pool streaming-node-3 at 2026-02-12T14:45:00Z :thumbsup:

rebecca_support: I'll ask customer to test mobile h2 path after we hit 1% (they can hit a specific route id we hand them).

jordan_se: For repro steps to give customer (quick): 
1) Run mobile client with http/2 and reproduce prompt < 20 tokens.
2) Capture request id header. 
3) Run curl fallback to non-streaming to compare times: 
```
time curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"stream":false,...}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
4) Then run streaming path with `-N` and compare TTFB. Also try forcing `Connection: close` to test connection reuse impact.

rebecca_support: Customer confirmed after 1% canary they saw p99 drop from ~2.1s -> ~420ms for the sampled requests. They want ETA on full fix. :relieved:

anya_dev: Next steps/action items: 
- mike_eng: complete canary grad to 100% for acme path and monitor 15m p99 -> target within 24h. (ETA 6h)
- infra: add edge check for `proxy_buffering` and document recommended settings for SSE vs h2. (ETA 48h)
- jordan_se: add router rule to fallback to non-streaming as emergency knob (opt-in flag). (ETA 72h)
- rebecca_support: keep customer updated and collect more rids if issue resurfaces.

mike_eng: I'll also open a small perf ticket to reevaluate default min_flush_tokens for rw-1 across tenants — balancing cost vs TTFB p99.

rebecca_support: great, thanks. I'll close this escalation once canary finishes and customer verifies stable. :thumbsup:

sam_ops: One more note: if customer sees chunk reordering on SSE during flaps, capture client side logs. That can be a downstream client event rather than server chunking.

rebecca_support: noted. Closing loop after 24h observation window.
